spec_match.rationale: Real window-drag: drag / no-drag declarations on a titlebar structure, now paired with a live probe of the exact surface: CSS.supports('window-drag','drag') plus the computed value on the drag zone, with the real runtime feature name (CSSWindowDrag, from runtime_enabled_features.json5) in the unsupported guidance.

interactive.rationale: The probe runs live on load and reports honestly; actual window-dragging remains a manual observation in an installed-app window (nothing a page can read back), which the supported-state text says explicitly. Fixed this pass from a fully static mock.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Lede now frames the mock as a rendering of the intended layout with the probe deciding what this engine really does.

edge_cases.rationale: Unsupported state (measured here: supports=false, computed empty) is disclosed with exact enable steps; supported state separates parse-success from the installed-app manual observation.

conformance.rationale: The probe mirrors the surface the feature suite checks.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CDP re-run after the fix: probe renders 'NOT SUPPORTED here — CSS.supports = false, computed (empty)' with CSSWindowDrag steps; also verified --enable-blink-features=CSSWindowDrag changes nothing on 141 (feature not in that build), matching the probe's honesty. 0px overflow both classes; zero console errors.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables; probe block on stone with charcoal text.

accessibility.rationale: Probe is a role=status live region; the decorative mock window controls are now aria-hidden and out of the tab order (fixed this pass).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×2000 (re-measured after fix).

summary: Re-reviewed after an in-place fix this pass (headless, no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): the formerly silent static mock now probes the exact CSS surface live, reports this engine's real unsupported state with the correct CSSWindowDrag steps (flag verified inert on 141), and neutralises its decorative controls for assistive tech.
